extracted.intended_audience: Prospective AAAI-24 authors and reviewers (AAAI conference submitters and program committee members)
extracted.subtask_description: Official AAAI-24 guidance describing the two-phase peer review process, double-blind submission requirements, citation/anonymous-work rules, author-feedback window, and related submission procedures for conference papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase 1: initial allocation and rejection criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Every paper will be allocated two reviewers. If a paper receives two reviews that are both sufficiently negative, it will be rejected without any opportunity for author feedback. Remaining papers will progress to Phase 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phase 1 serves as an initial triage: two sufficiently negative reviews -> summary rejection (no author feedback). 'Sufficiently negative' is the practical threshold used by the program chairs/committee to filter out clearly unsuitable submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase 2: additional reviewers and independent assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Each paper will be allocated additional reviewers. These reviewers will not be given access to Phase 1 reviews until after submitting their own reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phase 2 reviewers must form an independent judgment uninfluenced by Phase 1 text; access to Phase 1 reviews is withheld until the Phase 2 reviewer has submitted their review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author feedback window
rubrics_metrics.description: A single author feedback phase will give authors of papers from Phase 2 an opportunity to comment on all reviews (from both phases), running from November 2-5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author feedback is limited to this single window; the program committee and senior program committee will engage in a discussion phase taking author feedback into account before making final decisions (final decisions announced in December).

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-blind review requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: AAAI-24 reviews are double blind (i.e., neither reviewers nor authors should be able to identify each other).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The first page (where the paper body begins) may include title, abstract, content areas, and ID number (if available), but must not include names or affiliations of the authors. Acknowledgments of funding or assistance should be omitted. Ensure that no information is included that would identify the authors or their affiliations; papers including such information may be summarily rejected at the discretion of the program chairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to cite authors' previous work while preserving anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: When the authors’ previous work is relevant, authors have three options, in descending order of desirability: (1) Use the third person rather than the first person (e.g., 'Previously, Hinton et al (2006) showed that…' instead of 'In our previous work (Hinton et al, 2006) we showed that…'). (2) Avoid citing previous, unpublished work that would surely identify the authors (e.g., a previous technical report or PhD thesis which substantially overlaps with the current submission); such citations may be added to the camera-ready copy. (3) When neither previous option is appropriate, cite as 'Anonymous (2019)' to indicate that a citation has been suppressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer third-person citations of your own prior work. Do not include identifying unpublished citations in the submission; add them for camera-ready if needed. Use 'Anonymous (year)' only if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-anonymous online material exceptions and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two cases where the existence of non-anonymous online material will not be considered a violation of AAAI-24’s blind review policy: (1) preliminary versions as unrefereed preprints (e.g., on arXiv.org, social media, personal websites) or in any workshop that does not have archival proceedings; or (2) discussions in research talks, even if abstracts or videos of such talks are made available online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In these cases, the AAAI-24 submission should not include citations or other pointers to the non-anonymous material, and the non-anonymous online material should not reference the fact that the work was submitted to AAAI-24; violations may lead to summary rejection. Reviewers are instructed not to actively seek out such previous publications or to share knowledge of them with other reviewers, but reviewers will not be disqualified if they encounter such information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to include references to relevant published literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions should include references to all published literature relevant to the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must cite relevant published work; when citing their own prior relevant work, follow the anonymity guidance (third-person, suppress unpublished identifying work, or use 'Anonymous (year)').

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions for violating anonymity or citation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers including information that would identify the authors or their affiliations, or that violate the non-anonymous material rules, may be summarily rejected at the discretion of the program chairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly avoid names, affiliations, acknowledgments, and pointers to non-anonymous online material that would reveal identity; failing to do so risks summary rejection without review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and procedural submission requirements (deadlines and materials)
rubrics_metrics.description: Key dates and procedural requirements (examples listed): abstract deadline Aug 8, full paper deadline Aug 15, supplementary material and code due Aug 18, author feedback window Nov 2-5, notification and camera-ready timelines in December.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must meet the listed deadlines for abstracts, full papers, supplementary material, and camera-ready copies. Supplementary material and code must be uploaded by the stated deadline to be considered alongside the submission.
